issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify lectureName as a String attribute, but the solution implementation defines lectureName with type LectureName. This is an attribute type mismatch that will confuse students about the expected type and how to implement the constructor and getters/setters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the types across artifacts. Either change the solution to use a String for lectureName (and update constructor/getters/setters accordingly) to match the UML and template, or update the problem statement and template to declare lectureName as LectureName and document the new LectureName class and its intended usage.

issues.description: The solution's Lecture constructor takes a LectureName parameter, while the exercise description and UML indicate the constructor should accept and initialize a String lectureName (matching the attribute type in the specification). This constructor parameter mismatch will prevent students from following the specified constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter types consistent with the specification. Either change the solution constructor to accept a String lectureName (and assign to a String field), or update the problem statement/template to require a LectureName parameter and explain the LectureName type in the task description and UML.

issues.description: The solution's getter and setter for lectureName declare/use String signatures but operate on a LectureName field (getLectureName() is declared to return String yet returns the LectureName field; setLectureName(String) assigns a String to a LectureName field). This mismatch causes compilation errors and confuses students about the correct method signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure method signatures and field types are consistent. Either change the field type to String and keep getter/setter signatures that use String, or change getter/setter signatures to use LectureName (and adjust their implementations accordingly, e.g. return lectureName.toString() or lectureName.getValue() if a String result is desired). Update the UML and template accordingly if the LectureName type is intentionally introduced.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the attribute lectureName as a String, but the solution repository introduces a separate LectureName class and declares the lectureName field with type LectureName. This introduces a type/naming inconsistency for the same conceptual entity (the lecture's name) across artifacts and will confuse students mapping the requirement (a String lectureName) to the provided solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent representation for lectureName across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to use a plain String for lectureName to match the problem statement/UML — replace 'private LectureName lectureName;' with 'private String lectureName;', update the constructor and getter/setter signatures to accept and return String, and remove the LectureName helper class. Alternatively, if a LectureName wrapper is intended, update the problem statement and template to document and require LectureName so students see the same type everywhere.
